A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RADD research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original RADD language-modeling perplexities, generation quality, inference timings, sampling-order comparisons and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for revised RADD models, multiple training objectives and training budgets, together with generation experiments and appendix examples.

M1.justification: The time-independent RADD architecture and caching procedure remain. v2 explicitly fixes a missing time-independent LayerNorm bias (Section 4.3, footnote 2) and implements lambda-DCE and AO training variants alongside DSE and renamed t-DCE. The lambda and mask-count reformulations already appeared in v1; these are refinements of the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions train on OpenWebText and evaluate LAMBADA, WikiText2, PTB, WikiText103 and 1BW. Unconditional generation, generation conditioned on prefix and suffix prompts, and forward/backward/random-order sampling already occur in v1. Additional losses and training budgets do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The external zero-shot baseline families remain GPT-2, D3PM, PLAID and the SEDD variants. Internal model comparisons expand to RADD-lambda-DCE and RADD-AO; the sampling-order comparison replaces RADD-DSE with RADD-lambda-DCE (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). Newly discussed concurrent works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v1 uses a common SEDD training configuration; v2 changes non-DSE variants to weight decay 0.03 and dropout 0.02 while retaining the DSE control. It evaluates variants using their corresponding losses and reports separate 400k- and 1000k-iteration experiments. Appendix G.3 also revises RADD's generation sample count from 1000 to 1024. v1's total training iterations are unspecified, so a direct budget increase cannot be established.

E4.justification: The existing loss comparison broadens from DSE/DCE to four training variants, and Section 4.3 explicitly analyzes the matched DSE comparison as evidence about time conditioning. Appendix G.4 revises the models examined in the retained sampling-order analysis, and Figures 3–6 replace the qualitative examples. These extend existing analysis questions; the scaling-trick ablation remains.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages over generated samples or orders. Neither supplies training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many RADD results are replaced under revised model, training and evaluation conditions: RADD-DSE's LAMBADA entry changes from 96.62 to 51.83, and DCE/t-DCE's PTB entry from 116.74 to 109.03. Lambda-DCE, AO and 1000k-iteration results are added, while the SEDD-S 'exact likelihood' reevaluation disappears. RADD's 32-step generative perplexity changes from 135 to 158, with runtime values retained. The sampling-order winner changes from random to forward.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 changes from an exact diffusion negative-log-likelihood identity to equivalence among diffusion and any-order autoregressive objectives. v2 reuses parts of the lambda/mask-count derivations but adds the DSE-to-t-DCE equivalence proof (Appendix C.1), Euler/Tweedie equivalence under a log-linear schedule (D.4), and mean-parameterization analysis (E). Theorem 1's score factorization remains.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace exact-likelihood evaluation as a central contribution with diffusion/AO-ARM objective unification. The zero-shot contribution shifts from reevaluating SEDD to improved trained RADD variants. The sampling claim narrows from consistently better quality to similar quality while retaining the speedup claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 now acknowledges that different autoregressive orders generally define inconsistent distributions and interprets the objective as expected autoregressive negative log-likelihood and a diffusion likelihood bound. v2 also credits adopted hyperparameters for improved results and interprets the DSE comparison as supporting removal of time conditioning. The GPT-2-scale and fixed-length-output limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a RADD code-access link, explicit training budgets and regularization settings, the LayerNorm-bias correction, lambda-DCE pseudocode, and disclosure that sampling uses no top-p/top-k annealing. The hardware description changes from 16 V100/A100 GPUs to nodes with 32 V100 GPUs. Earlier attention/checkpointing details and the SEDD URL/license appendix are removed, materially changing reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds the AO-ARM research lineage and substantial discussion of concurrent work by Shi et al. and Sahoo et al. Section 5 distinguishes overlapping losses, time-conditioning findings and caching from RADD's theoretical contributions, and credits Shi et al.'s hyperparameters. This substantially revises contribution positioning, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The background is reorganized around continuous-time diffusion and AO-ARMs, Section 3.3 is extensively rewritten, and the introduction and experimental narrative are recast. The main-text NFE derivation is shortened, theorem proofs are regrouped, and the sampling appendix is reorganized into dedicated subsections. These are substantial structural and explanatory revisions.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is simplified from four curves to two with a revised legend and caption. The zero-shot table is regrouped, a separate training-budget table is added, and the runtime table moves to Appendix G.4. The license table disappears and sample figures are replaced. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The decisive improvement is replacing v1's central exact-likelihood overclaim with the bound/expected-AO-likelihood distinction and explicitly acknowledging order inconsistency (Theorem 2; Section 3.3). The disclosed model repair, clearer experimental configurations and substantive concurrent-work discussion further improve reliability. Changed regularization limits attribution of performance gains, and some implementation/license detail is lost, but these tradeoffs do not outweigh the central conceptual correction.
